newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices even to softer.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices even to softer.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were flat to down 1/8 point in quiet midday trade, market sources said.

"It kind of feels like people are bracing for year end, so there hasn't been a lot of trading this morning," a trader said, adding that prices were about 1/8 point softer. "I'd say prices are probably down a little bit, and the bid is kind of thin."
A second trader judged muni prices unchanged.
"I would say they were unchanged just because there is no activity," he said. "This probably has to be the slowest day I've seen this year not counting a holiday type weekend day. It's frightening."

Actively quoted secondary issues included Dade County, Fla., 5-1/2 percent water and sewer system revenue bonds of October 2025. The bonds had 5.69 percent net bid, versus a 5.67 percent net bid on Friday. Texas Turnpike Authority Dallas North Tollway 5-1/4 percent bonds of January 2023 had a 5.64 percent net bid, unchanged from Friday.
"Customers are kind of quiet," a trader said. "There's some bonds out for the bid, but certainly nothing overwhelming."

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was down 12/32 at 98-20/32 to yield 6.61 percent. In debt futures, the March municipal contract was down 1/32 at 115-17/32. The March T-bond contract 8/32 at 113. The MOB spread was 81 ticks.
On the economic front, the Federal Reserve board reported that U.S. industrial production rose 0.9 percent in November against a 0.2 percent drop in October.
Economists polled by Reuters had expected a 0.6 percent gain. Capacity utilization was also above expectations at 83.3 percent in November, up from 82.9 in October.
Turning to new issues, Lehman Brothers is expected to price a $626 million New York City offering on Tuesday.
"The big deal this week is the city deal, and it looks like it's fairly light after this week through the end of the year," a trader said.
New York City's deal included, 44 negotiated offerings totaling $2.46 billion are expected this week.

Competitive sales total $680 million in 65 issues. The largest scheduled issue was Monday's $130 million King County, Wash., deal. Goldman Sachs & Co was the winner at a true interest cost of 5.59 percent.
